First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{2x-1} & =3\cdot {8}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{2x-1}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot {8}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
2x-1=\operatorname{ln}⁡(3\cdot {8}^{x}).
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({8}^{x}) \\ 2x-1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-1 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) \\ 2x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)+1 \\ 2x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(8) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+1 \\ x(2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+1 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(3)+1}{2-\operatorname{ln}⁡(8)}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{4x} & ={4}^{1-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{1-x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
4x=\operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{1-x}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
4x=(1-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =(1-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ 4x & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ 4x+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x(4+\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{4+\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{3x} & ={9}^{6-x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({7}^{3x}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{6-x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)=(6-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =(6-x)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ 3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x(3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x & =\frac{6\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡(7)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)}\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{7x+3} & ={10}^{x+8} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({4}^{7x+3}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({10}^{x+8})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}(7x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(x+8)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(7x+3)\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =(x+8)\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ 7x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)+8\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ 7x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x(7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)) & =8\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4) \\ x & =\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)-3\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)}{7\operatorname{ln}⁡(4)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}\end{aligned}
$$
